hints: Focus on how the carbons split between the acid part and the alcohol part in an ester, since total carbons must add to 5.
Work out which alcohol must pair with each acid, ethanoic acid needs a C3 alcohol, propanoic acid needs a C2 alcohol, and butanoic acid needs a C1 alcohol.
Remember to count how many structural isomers each alcohol has, as each different alcohol gives a different ester.
walkthrough:
**Write the ester rule**

Think of an ester as acid carbons plus alcohol carbons joined together with water lost. The total carbon count is conserved.

$$\text{carbons in acid (n) + carbons in alcohol (m) = carbons in ester = 5}$$

**Match each acid to its alcohol partner**

Ethanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ with n = 2, so it needs m = 3, a propanol. Propanoic acid has n = 3, so it needs m = 2, ethanol. Butanoic acid has n = 4, so it needs m = 1, methanol.

**Count how many esters each acid can make**

The key is alcohol isomerism. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH}$ has two isomers, propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol, so ethanoic acid makes two esters. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ has only ethanol and $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ has only methanol, so both propanoic and butanoic acids make one ester only.

Conclusion: statements 2 and 3 are correct, statement 1 is not.

options.A: Incorrect. This means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong because ethanoic acid (C2) pairs with a C3 alcohol, and there are two propanols, giving two different C5 esters, not one only.
options.B: Incorrect. This means 1 and 2 only. Statement 1 fails for the reason above, while statement 3 is actually correct and is missing here. Butanoic acid (C4) needs methanol (C1) which has no isomers, so it gives one ester only.
options.C: Correct. This means 2 and 3 only. Propanoic acid (C3) needs ethanol (C2, only one isomer) to give ethyl propanoate. Butanoic acid (C4) needs methanol (C1, only one isomer) to give methyl butanoate. Both give one ester only.
options.D: Incorrect. This means 1 only. Ethanoic acid gives propyl ethanoate with propan-1-ol and 1-methylethyl ethanoate with propan-2-ol, so it gives two esters of formula C5H10O2, not one only.
